page.layout: One page of running text in a single column; below it a centred ornament, then the chapter heading "CAP. LXXXVII." with its summary line in smaller type; at the foot, a catchword at the right.

main_text.p: ipsi Domini nostri Iefu Christi discipuli, ubiq; commendat & approbat Tertullianus, maxime in lib. aduersus Praxeam, in fine. & libro De monogamia. 8 Hominem Christianam bona conscientia sub principe suo, si sit ethnicus, militare posse negat, & usum armorum omnino Christianis interdicit, imo vero etiam eos iudices quos vocant, capitales & criminales esse vetat, in libro De idololatria, quia usum gladij Christianis adimit. Hoc Anabaptistas peperit, in hoc errore pertinacissimos[?]. Itaque iampridem Tertulliani opuscula damnata sunt, communi quodam consensu Ecclesiae, vt appareret ex Can.Sancta.distinct.15. Quaedam autem tribuuntur Tertulliano, quae non sunt erronea, veluti quòd panem & vinum in Coena Domini figuram & σύμβολα[?] corporis & sanguinis ipsius esse dixerit in libro 4. aduersus Marcionem. Sed sic Papae etiam ipsi sunt loquuti, vti Hilarius 2. in Canone Corpus Christi. De Consecr. distinct.2. vt intelligant Papistae quantum à capitis sui doctrina discesserint. Quaedam etiam dure de Trinitate & distinctione Personarum diuinarum dixit. Itaque cum magno iudicio legendus est Tertullianus: quemadmodum etiam veteres Patres scriptores Ecclesiastici pene omnes.
main_text.head: CAP. LXXXVII. Abelonitæ cur sic dicti. Erroris autem eorum caput vnum.

page.notes: The Greek word after "figuram &" is printed in the Greek letters σύμβολα; the scan is faint, so the reading is doubtful. "pertinacissimos" is hard to read at the abbreviation; the scan may show a q-form abbreviation. Paragraph breaks in the main text are not clear from the scan, so the text is given as one continuous paragraph. The running head is set in spaced capitals. Faint show-through from the reverse side and stains in the margins are left out.
